analysis: The broad option anchors planning inquiry in applied spatial projects, GIS, climate and water, then connects those skills with sociology, statistics, policy and governance. It directly addresses geospatial evidence and competing claims without claiming professional design studios.

The environmental option develops hazard and adaptation analysis, geospatial techniques, delta water management, soils, coastal ecology and energy design. This gives a sustained environmental and physical direction, while the dedicated planning studios remain distinct.

The governance option anchors institutional questions in applied spatial projects. Law, public policy, economics, participation and sustainability governance examine decisions about land, resources and environmental risk. It is a policy emphasis with spatial applications, rather than professional planning-law formation.

academicConstruction: Resolved eight original offering conflicts. Economics moves to term one in all options. Earth System Science Tools moves to term six in the broad option, while two unavailable versions of Research in a Sustainable Delta leave the schedules. Dynamic Earth moves to term three in the climate option, which adds Marine Biology and Spatial Planning. The governance option removes Consumer Product Design and adds both sustainability gateways, Spatial Planning and Public Policy Analysis. Earth Observation remains in the broad and environmental options. All three include eight advanced courses and differ by ten, nine and seventeen courses per pair in each direction. Spatial Planning and Public Policy Analysis make direct contributions within their documented descriptions. Their course titles do not establish design-atelier or specialist planning-law equivalence.
